questions.text: In a fuel cell methanol is used as fuel and oxygen gas is used as an oxidizer. The reaction is $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{OH}(\ell)+\frac{3}{2} \mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{~g}) \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})+2 \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}(\ell)$ At 298K standard Gibb's energies of formation for $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{OH}(\ell), \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}(\ell)$ and $\mathrm{CO}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})$ are $-166.2,-237.2$ and $-394.4 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ respectively. If standard enthalpy of combustion of methanol is $-726 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$, efficiency of the fuel cell will be

options.D:
97\%

Sol: (4)
$$\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{OH}(\ell)+\frac{3}{2} \mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{~g}) \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})+2 \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}(\ell) \quad \Delta \mathrm{H}=-726 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$$

Also $\Delta \mathrm{G}_{\mathrm{f}}^{\circ} \mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{OH}(\ell)=-166.2 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\Delta \mathrm{G}_{\mathrm{f}}^{\circ} \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}(\ell)=-237.2 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \\
\Delta \mathrm{G}_{\mathrm{f}}^{\circ} \mathrm{CO}_{2}(\ell)=-394.4 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}
\end{array}$$
$\because \Delta \mathrm{G}=\Sigma \Delta \mathrm{G}_{\mathrm{f}}^{\circ}$ products $-\Sigma \Delta \mathrm{G}_{\mathrm{f}}^{\circ}$ reactants.
$$\begin{array}{l}
=-394.4-2(237.2)+166.2 \\
=-702.6 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}
\end{array}$$
now Efficiency of fuel cell $=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{G}}{\Delta \mathrm{H}} \times 100$
$$\begin{array}{l}
=\frac{702.6}{726} \times 100 \\
=97 \%
\end{array}$$

questions.text: Given : $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{Fe}^{3+} / \mathrm{Fe}}^{\circ}=-0.036 \mathrm{~V}, \quad \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{Fe}^{2+} / \mathrm{Fe}}^{\circ}=-0.439 \mathrm{~V}$. The value of standard electrode potential for the change, $\mathrm{Fe}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{3+}+\mathrm{e}^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Fe}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq})$ will be :

options.D:
-0.270

Sol: (3)
$$\begin{array}{l}
\because \mathrm{Fe}^{3+}+3 \mathrm{e}^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Fe} ; \mathrm{E}^{\circ}=-0.036 \mathrm{~V} \\
\therefore \Delta \mathrm{G}_{1}^{\circ}=-\mathrm{nFE}^{\circ}=-3 \mathrm{~F}(-0.036) \\
=+0.108 \mathrm{~F}
\end{array}$$

Also $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}+2 \mathrm{e}^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Fe} ; \mathrm{E}^{\circ}=-0.439 \mathrm{~V}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\therefore \Delta G_{2}^{\circ}=-n F E^{\circ} \\
=-2 F(-0.439) \\
=0.878 F
\end{array}$$

To find $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}$ for $\mathrm{Fe}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{3+}+\mathrm{e}^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Fe}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq})$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\Delta G^{\circ}=-n F E^{\circ} \\
=-1 F E^{\circ} \\
\because G^{\circ}=G_{1}^{\circ}-G_{2}^{\circ} \\
\therefore G^{\circ}=0.108 F-0.878 F \\
\therefore-F E^{\circ}=+0.108 F-0.878 F \\
\therefore E^{\circ}=0.878-0.108 \\
=0.77 v
\end{array}$$

any integer

Sol: (3)
$$\begin{array}{l}
\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
a & a+1 & a-1 \\
-b & b+1 & b-1 \\
c & c-1 & c+1
\end{array}\right|+(-1)^{n}\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
a+1 & b+1 & c-1 \\
a-1 & b-1 & c+1 \\
a & -b & c

a & a+1 & a-1 \\
-b & b+1 & b-1 \\
c & c-1 & c+1
\end{array}\right|+(-1)^{n}\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
a+1 & a-1 & a \\
b+1 & b-1 & -b \\
c-1 & c+1 & c
\end{array}\right| \\
=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
a & a+1 & a-1 \\
-b & b+1 & b-1 \\
c & c-1 & c+1
\end{array}\right|+(-1)^{n+1}\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
a+1 & a & a-1 \\
b+1 & -b & b-1 \\
c-1 & c & c+1

a & a+1 & a-1 \\
-b & b+1 & b-1 \\

\end{array}$$

This is equal to zero only if $\mathrm{n}+2$ is odd i.e. n is odd integer.

=\int_{0}^{\pi}[\cot (\pi-x)] d x=\int_{0}^{\pi}[-\cot x] d x

2 \mathrm{I}=\int_{0}^{\pi}[\cot \mathrm{x}] \mathrm{dx}+\int_{0}^{\pi}[-\cot \mathrm{x}] \mathrm{dx}==\int_{0}^{\pi}(-1) \mathrm{dx} \\
=[-\mathrm{x}]_{0}^{\pi}=-\pi \\
\therefore \mathrm{I}=-\frac{\pi}{2}
\end{array}$$

Now $f^{\prime}(x)=3 x^{2}+5>0, \forall x \in R$
$\therefore \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})$ is strictly increasing function

$\therefore f(x)$ takes every value between $-\infty$ and $\infty$.
